text: UT Dallas > Office of the Registrar > Legislative Policies > Vaccination Requirement – Bacterial Meningitis Vaccination Requirement – Bacterial Meningitis About Bacterial Meningitis. Bacterial Meningitis is a serious, potentially deadly disease that can progress extremely fast. It is an inflammation of the membranes that surround the brain and spinal cord. The bacterium that causes meningitis can also infect the blood. For more information, please review the About Bacterial Meningitis information.

Per Texas Senate Bill no. 62, beginning January 1, 2014, all entering students under the age of 22 enrolling at a Texas college or university must show proof of a bacterial meningitis vaccination or booster (if the original vaccination is five years old) at least 10 days before the first day of class. Failure to receive vaccination by the deadline dates below will prevent you from attending classes for the term. Acceptable Proof of Vaccination Documentation must:

Include student’s full name and other identifying information (i.e date of birth) Show the month, date and year of vaccination. Be within the five years prior to and no later than 10 days before the first day of the term. Be one of the following: Documentation of vaccines administered that include the signature or stamp of the physician or physician’s designee, or public health personnel, is acceptable. Office of the Registrar. Immunization records generated from electronic health record systems must include clinic contact information and the provider’s signature/stamp. An official immunization record generated from a state or local health authority. An official record received from school officials, including a record from another state.

To attend classes, you must submit: 1. A completed Meningococcal Meningitis Vaccine Requirement Form (pdf). 2. Proof of vaccination or a notarized Affidavit for Exemption from Immunizations for Reasons of Submission Deadline by Term. Your vaccine must be administered within five years prior to and no later than 10 days before the first day of the term. Spring 2027 Term – Meningitis vaccine must be taken between January 19, 2022 and January 9, 2027. Summer 2027 Term – Meningitis vaccine must be taken between June 1, 2022 and May 22, 2027. Fall 2027 Term – Meningitis vaccine must be taken between August 23, 2022 and August 13, 2027.

1. Log in to Orion. galaxy.utdallas.edu 2. Click on “Admissions Forms” tile, 3. Select Vaccination Requirement – Bacterial Meningitis. 4. Click on “Submit Meningitis Vaccine” 5. text: You decline for reasons of conscience or religious belief by submitting an affidavit. Affidavits. In Texas, there are two ways to obtain an immunization exemption affidavit for reasons of conscience (including religious beliefs): 1. Download the blank affidavit form directly from the Texas Department of State Health Services (DSHS) website. A child’s parent, a legal guardian, or a student 18 years or older has the option to download and print the blank immunization exemption affidavit form. The form must be completed, notarized, and submitted to the Office of the Registrar. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/immunizations/school/exemptions 2. Request a hard copy of the affidavit from the Texas Department of State Health Services. Individuals may submit a request online, by mail, fax, or in person. Texas DSHS will mail the official affidavit form to the address provided.

Please see below to request a hard copy exemption affidavit by one of these methods: Secure online request form for exemption affidavit Fax: (512) 776-7544 In person: Texas Department of State Health Services (DSHS)

1100 West 49th Street Austin, TX 78756. All affidavits must be notarized by a Texas notary. If requesting the original hard copy affidavit to be mailed to you, UT Dallas can only accept the orignal hard copy. Both affidavits serve the same purpose; the difference is how the affidavits are obtained. Once completed and notarized, the affidavits must be submitted according to Texas immunization exemption requirements. Where to Get Vaccinated: Collin County Dallas County Denton County
